In summary, our research is concerned with

the morphological and neuroendocrine characterization of neurons projecting to the larval ring gland of Protophormiata terraenovae, which is an intermediate host for human tapeworm, Diphyllobothrium latum.
the morphology of the cephalic neurohemal organs and their innervation in the larval blow flies, Protophromia terraenovoe.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cephalic neurosecretory system of the larva is composed of three types of neurons, viz., those projecting to the ring glands, those projecting to the aorta, and those projecting to both organs.

the larval blowfly, P. terraenovae, has a cephalic neurosecretory system that regulates the ring gland and possibly other organs by releasing neurohormones and/or neuromodulators into the hemolymb and/or locally into the ring gland and other organs.

the larval ring gland is innervated by neurons with somata located in the PI, PL and SEG of the central nervous system, and that these neurons may release cholecystokin-8, FMFRamide, and pigment dispersing factor-like peptides as neurohormone candidates to regulate the production of hormones by the cells of the ring gland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ring gland is innervated by a large number of neurons, and that the gland is under the control of both intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

the ring gland and the aorta in the larval blowfly, Protophorphia terraenovaa, are innervated by at least three types of neurons: (i) neurons with somatas in the pars intercerbralis (PI), pars lateralis (PI) and subesophageal (SEG) ganglia; (ii) neurons with ipsilateral projections in the PI and (iii) contralateral projections in the PL.
the ring gland and the aorta receive a variety of inputs from the brain, which may regulate the activity of the gland cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a large number of neurons that project to the ring gland, and that they are heterogeneous.
the larval brain of Protophorma terraenovae has a well-developed cephalic neurosecretory system.

the ring gland of the larval fly, Protophorima terraenovae, is innervated by a variety of neurons that are located in the protocerebral pars intercerebalis, pars lateralis and the subesophagean ganglion.
